name: Sharia
summary: Sharia is the religious law of Islam: a divinely ordained path of duties toward God and other people, drawn from the Quran, the Sunnah, scholarly consensus and analogy. It covers ritual, family, inheritance, commercial and criminal law, with fixed (hadd) punishments for a handful of crimes, a ban on interest, and a patriarchal family law. Its interpretation varies by school, and most modern states apply it only to family law.
scope: The traditional (classical) sharia as Britannica's article on the sharia (Noel James Coulson) describes it, resting on the four sources it names, with the Quran as the primary text. It excludes modern Islamist programmes, the codes of any one state, and the rulings of any single school where the sources do not state them.

keyWorks.title: Qurʾan
keyWorks.quote: The main sources of the sharia (Islamic law) are the Qurʾan , Sunnah , ijmāʿ , and qiyās .
